title: What has to be true before a cell divides

objectives.statement: Given a named cell-cycle transition, state the physical condition a checkpoint detects there, name the molecular activity that is withheld while the condition is unsatisfied, and explain why the length of a resulting hold is set by the detected state rather than by elapsed time.

From a measured proliferative fraction and a tissue turnover time, derive the average cycle time of a renewing tissue's proliferative compartment, state the steady-state assumptions the derivation rests on, show why the tissue's total cell count cancels out, and say what the result implies about the relative division rates of stem and transit-amplifying cells.

Place the events of mitosis and cytokinesis in order by the condition each one depends on, name the molecular step that makes sister-chromatid separation irreversible, and use that irreversibility to explain where in the sequence surveillance has to act.

Given a described error of chromosome attachment, segregation or cytokinesis, predict whether a functional checkpoint will detect it, justify the prediction by naming the physical variable a detector would have to read, name the resulting abnormality in the daughter cell, and distinguish claims about missegregation that are established from those that are disputed or unit-dependent.

Explain how a colonic crypt sustains hundreds of divisions a day from about seven slowly dividing stem cells, show by calculation that an amplifying compartment is arithmetically necessary, and state what neutral drift predicts about the fate of a lineage arising in a single crypt stem cell.

scenes.title: Two hundred divisions a day, in one crypt
A checkpoint is a condition, not a clock
How long one turn of the cycle has to take
One unattached kinetochore, and the whole cell waits
The spindle decides where the cut goes
A checkpoint a wrong answer can satisfy
Practice: budget it, then predict what gets through
Clinical wrap-up: the drug found the crypt without being aimed at it
